[SA08-C910] A determination theorem needs continuity/density conditions or a restricted functor category. Over a field, evaluation followed by identity and algebraic double dual agree on finite-dimensional tests but differ on infinite-dimensional values; mere additivity is insufficient.

[SA08-C911] Finite-dimensional duality identifies the two expressions over a field; infinite algebraic biduality does not. Cochain reconstruction must retain a continuous dual/topology, finite-projective hypothesis, or the original representable functor. This is an obstruction to the proposed shortcut, not to Yoneda.

statement:
[SA08-C924] Normalized chains of the diagonal of a multisimplicial object and the total normalized multicomplex are naturally chain-homotopy equivalent. Shuffle is associative and symmetric with Koszul signs; AW is coassociative and generally not symmetric. These maps provide the cup product and K(A,i)⊗K(B,j)→K(A⊗B,i+j).

[SA08-C926] Dold1961 Theorem1.6 concerns natural transformations in an ordered n-tuple of independently varying FD complexes. This natural-Hom complex is acyclic over Z. Sections1.7–1.12 choose a separate positive Z[pi]-free resolution W and construct W→Hom; they do not assert Hom is free. Specializing all inputs afterward gives equivariant operations. If the manuscript instead means all transformations natural only in one diagonal variable X, the claimed H0=Z is false: for n=2 the four natural coordinate maps X²→X² remain linearly independent on a two-point discrete X, where no chain homotopies are possible.

[SA08-C927] A free group-ring resolution and an equivariant acyclic-model operation construction produce the higher cochain operations in each arity. To infer an E∞ algebra one must additionally check compatible operadic composition across arities. The displayed sketches alone do not perform that check.
